GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2020-07-23T17:53:41Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Default checkpoint location problematic when using docker 
Description: The default behavior of `ModelCheckpoint` is to use `os.getcwd()`. Outside my docker container, this ended up being the same directory where my tensorboard logs were saved (e.g. `/my/dir/tb_logs/default/version_0/checkpoints/`).  But inside the docker container, it saved to the internal working directory (e.g. `/home/default/version_0/checkpoints/`). Since this location disappeared along with the container, the checkpoint was gone, and there was no warning raised to explain why.

Requiring a checkpoint directory isn't desirable, but I'd like to help others avoid this grief in the future. Is there a better way to infer a default location than `os.getcwd()`? Something as simple as a print statement with the checkpoint location would have saved me a lot of time troubleshooting.

llm_response:
CATEGORY: 1
REASONING: This issue is about the default behavior of `ModelCheckpoint` using `os.getcwd()` which causes problems in Docker environments where checkpoints are saved to ephemeral container locations. The issue is conceptual and relates to how the library handles default paths. No build environment is needed to verify the solution, which would likely involve either:

1. Modifying the default behavior to use a more persistent location
2. Adding a warning/print statement showing where checkpoints are being saved
3. Improving documentation about checkpoint locations in containerized environments

This is fundamentally a design/documentation issue about path handling that can be analyzed and verified without running any code. The solution would involve reviewing the code that sets default paths and potentially modifying it to be more container-friendly or to provide better feedback to users.
